Re: Appeal of denial for CPT 29806  
Reference number: POC-65BD57974D-81336  
Requested service: Shoulder labral/instability repair  

Dear Wellpoint Maryland Grievances and Appeals Department:

I appeal the denial dated August 8, 2026, for arthroscopic shoulder capsulorrhaphy and labral/instability repair, CPT 29806. The denial states that the submitted documentation was incomplete and did not allow a determination of medical necessity.

The submitted clinical information supports medical necessity and addresses the criteria in the Carelon Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines Musculoskeletal Appropriate Use Criteria: Joint Surgery, document MSK02-1125.1, effective November 15, 2025. The guideline identifies the following criterion:

“Shoulder pain and/or instability which interferes with age-appropriate activities of daily living”

This criterion is supported by the records. I have experienced recurrent shoulder instability for 14 months, including three anterior dislocations. The most recent dislocation required reduction in the emergency department. I avoid overhead reaching and cannot return to work involving lifting.

The guideline also states:

“Physical exam consistent with symptomatic glenohumeral instability (e.g., apprehension, relocation, load and shift)”

The orthopedic examination documents positive apprehension and relocation tests and increased anterior translation on load-and-shift testing. These findings objectively demonstrate symptomatic anterior glenohumeral instability. Strength is full, which does not negate the documented mechanical instability.

The guideline further identifies MRI evidence including:

“A labral lesion consistent with the clinical instability”

The June 11, 2026 MR arthrogram demonstrates an anteroinferior labral tear, also known as a Bankart lesion, with a small Hill-Sachs lesion. These findings are consistent with the recurrent anterior dislocations and examination findings. The imaging also documents glenoid bone loss under 10 percent and an intact rotator cuff.

The records also establish failure of conservative treatment. I completed 12 weeks of supervised physical therapy from March 29, 2026, through June 21, 2026, consisting of 24 visits focused on rotator cuff and scapular stabilizer strengthening, together with activity modification. I also used NSAIDs for four months during flares. Despite this treatment, recurrent instability continued, including another dislocation requiring emergency reduction. No injection was indicated because the problem is instability rather than an inflammatory pain condition.

The clinical documentation also addresses relevant safety and treatment considerations. There is no active infection or untreated substance use. BMI is 29, the patient is a nonsmoker, and the rotator cuff is intact. Okafor, MD, orthopedic surgeon, has requested the procedure to treat the documented recurrent instability and Bankart lesion.

The Carelon guideline states that clinical documentation must “accurately reflect the clinical situation at the time of the requested service” and “sufficiently document the ordering provider’s clinical intent.” The enclosed records provide the relevant history, functional impairment, physical examination, imaging, failed conservative care, and treatment rationale. They should permit a medical-necessity determination.

Please overturn the denial and authorize CPT 29806. If Wellpoint believes that additional information is required, please identify specifically which criterion or document remains unmet and provide the exact clinical-review criteria and materials used for this determination. Please also arrange a peer-to-peer review with Okafor, MD, if necessary.

Please process this as a timely appeal received before the February 4, 2027 deadline. I request written confirmation of receipt and the appeal determination.

Sincerely,

Sawyer Foster  
Member ID: W356952515  

Enclosures:

- Denial notice dated August 8, 2026  
- MR arthrogram report dated June 11, 2026  
- Orthopedic examination and surgical recommendation  
- Physical therapy discharge note documenting 24 visits from March 29, 2026, through June 21, 2026  
- Documentation of recurrent dislocations and emergency-department reduction  
- Medication and conservative-treatment history  
- Relevant medical records addressing infection, substance use, BMI, smoking status, and rotator-cuff status
